$comment: Vulnerabilities we have reviewed and accepted, so CI fails only on NEW ones.
A scanner that is permanently red is a scanner everyone learns to ignore.
Each entry needs a real reason and an expiry date. On expiry the build fails
until someone re-reviews it — that is the point: an accepted risk should be
revisited, not buried. Delete an entry the moment the fix lands upstream.
`id` is the npm advisory id shown by `npm audit --json` (via[].source).

allow.title: Stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs
allow.reason: Reached only through prisma -> @prisma/config, the CLI's config loader. It parses our own prisma.config.ts at build/CLI time and never runs in a request. npm's only fix is prisma@6.19.3 — a DOWNGRADE from 7.x that would break schema.prisma, which uses the v7-only `prisma-client` generator with a required `output` path.

allow.title: Auth plugin downgrade to mysql_clear_password leaks plaintext credentials
allow.reason: This project talks to Postgres through @prisma/adapter-pg. mysql2 arrives as an unused driver inside prisma's dependency tree and is never loaded, so there is no MySQL connection to downgrade. Same prisma@6 downgrade problem as above.

allow.title: Unbounded zlib inflate in compressed MySQL protocol handler (decompression bomb)
allow.reason: Same as 1153173 — no MySQL connection exists, so the protocol handler never runs.
